claims.text: PCC-WFE (Pearson-correlation-coefficient weighted feature expansion) adds one new feature to the 178 raw EEG features, giving Dataset 2 with 179 features.
On Dataset 2 (PCC-WFE expanded), XGBoost reaches the highest 10-fold accuracy among the four traditional classifiers (XGBoost 0.9513 > RF 0.9432 > DT 0.9239 > SVM 0.878).
PCC-WFE improves the traditional classifiers relative to the raw 178-feature data (Dataset 1).
The SGRU classifier outperforms the plain GRU classifier on Dataset 1 (ACC 97.33 vs 92.76, Se 88.89 vs 78.86, PPV 97.51 vs 96.45).
The SGRU classifier outperforms the plain GRU classifier on Dataset 2 (ACC 97.43 vs 94.19, Se 89.86 vs 81.13, PPV 97.93 vs 96.70).
SGRU on Dataset 2 is the best overall configuration (ACC 97.43%), above every traditional classifier and above GRU.
The dataset is balanced: 2300 samples in each of the 5 classes.
The capsule reproduces the published results by running `run` (NewData_ML_Kfold.py plus the fig_*.py scripts).

findings.evidence: The UCI Epileptic Seizure Recognition set contains 500 segments per patient (23 patients, 5 classes x 100 segments each). The code splits the 11500 rows with a plain KFold over rows, so segments of the same patient appear in both training and test folds. The capsule does not report a patient identifier or a grouped split.
findings.question_for_authors: Were the folds grouped by patient? If not, how much of the reported accuracy comes from patient overlap between training and test?

findings.location: code/PCC_WFE.py load_data (pc(X, y_data) over all 11500 rows)
findings.evidence: The PCC-WFE new feature is built from the Pearson correlation between each of the 178 features and the label computed on the full dataset, before the 10-fold split. The label therefore enters the construction of a predictor that is then evaluated on held-out folds, and the MinMaxScaler is likewise fitted on all rows.
findings.question_for_authors: Was the PCC weighting recomputed inside each training fold? If not, what is the accuracy when it is?

findings.evidence: No random seed is set in any script (no np.random.seed / random_state / tf seed), yet the reported per-fold accuracies are single-run values. KFold(n_splits=10) is used without shuffle, so the fold assignment is deterministic, but XGBoost, RF, DT and the Keras models are not.
findings.question_for_authors: What seeds were used for the tree ensembles and the Keras models, and what is the run-to-run spread of the reported accuracies?

No open-access full text of the article could be located (Crossref and OpenAlex title/author queries returned no record of this exact title). The paper text used here is the capsule metadata, code/README.md, REPRODUCING.md, results/output and the figure scripts. Every paper-level claim (reported tables, abstract numbers, stated methods) is therefore unverifiable and marked grey.
findings.question_for_authors: Please provide the DOI or a full-text link of the published article so its tables can be compared with the capsule output.

findings.evidence: The traditional classifiers report Se and PPV as macro averages over the two binarised classes (metrics.recall_score(..., average='macro')), while the SGRU/GRU path uses perform.py, which computes Se = TP/(TP+FN) and PPV = TP/(TP+FP) for the seizure class only. The two metric definitions are not the same quantity, so the Se/PPV columns of the traditional and deep models are not directly comparable.
findings.question_for_authors: Were the Se/PPV values of the traditional classifiers and of SGRU/GRU computed with the same definition?

findings.evidence: The Keras models are fitted with the test fold passed as validation_data, and the reported scores are computed on that same fold. No early stopping or checkpoint selection is used in the released code, so the test fold does not influence training directly, but the released code does not show whether a model-selection step used it.
findings.question_for_authors: Was the test fold used only for monitoring, or also for model selection?

findings.evidence: With the paper's own choices the claim 'On the PCC-WFE expanded data, XGBoost has the highest 10-fold accuracy of the four traditional classifiers' does not hold on re-run (effect = -0.03356521739130436).
